prompt: Write an email to a colleague about a recent trip to town and who you met there. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Notes from my trip into town

Hi Jordan,

I hope your week is going well. I wanted to give you a quick rundown of my trip into town last Thursday, since a few of the conversations are relevant to what we've been working on.

The main reason for going was the regional planning meeting at the civic center. I'd expected a dry morning of slide decks, but it turned out to be quite useful. I arrived early and ended up chatting over coffee with Maria Delgado, who runs operations for the county's transportation office. She mentioned that their team is about to open a round of small grants for community infrastructure projects, and she thought our proposal on the riverside walkway might be a strong fit. She offered to send over the application guidelines, and I told her we'd be glad to take a look. I'd suggest we start sketching a budget outline this week so we're not scrambling when the window opens.

During the break I also met David Okafor, an engineer from a local firm called Brightline Consulting. He's done a lot of surveying and drainage work along the river, which is exactly the area we've been worried about. He was generous with his time and walked me through some of the common flooding problems he's seen in similar projects. He offered to look over our site plan informally, no strings attached. I took his card and said I'd follow up. It might be worth having him join one of our upcoming calls.

After lunch, I sat in on a panel about funding and partnerships. The most interesting speaker was Priya Raman, who leads a small nonprofit focused on public green spaces. She described how her group partnered with the city on a similar project, and she was candid about what went well and what slowed them down. The biggest lesson was to involve neighbors early, since community support made a real difference when they went to the council for approval. I'd like to pick her brain further, and she seemed open to a call.

On the way out, I stopped by the planning office to pick up the zoning maps we'd discussed. The staff member at the counter, Tom, was very helpful and said he could answer questions if we run into anything confusing. I've scanned the maps and will save them to our shared folder.

Overall, it was a worthwhile day. If you have time on Monday, could we grab twenty minutes to go over next steps? I'd like to get emails out to Maria, David, and Priya before the end of the week.

Thanks,
[name]
